title: Regional canary publishing and timezone-aware release scheduling for performance profiles
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Rationale:
We publish Redwood-verified performance profiles globally today, but the publish flow assumes a single release time and a homogeneous validation set. Customers in APAC/EU see regressions when a profile published during N. America daytime is rolled out without region-specific canaries. This ticket defines a schedule and canary strategy that is timezone-aware, region-aware, and ties publish rollout progression to telemetry-based health checks and cost anchors.

Goals:
- Add region-scoped canary phases for profile publish (NA / EU / APAC) with configurable mirror and shadow traffic percentages.
- Introduce timezone-aware publish windows so automated publishes avoid local peak hours and align canaries with regional SRE on-call schedules.
- Define telemetry-driven gates (latency P99, throughput degrade %, cost per token delta) to automatically advance/rollback rollouts.
- Surface a publish dashboard entry for each region with canary health and regional rollback action.

Out of scope:
- Rewriting the full verification harness (this will reuse existing verification agents).
- Permanent changes to pricing model (cost anchors are monitoring-only for the rollout decision).

Notes on urgency:
- Several enterprise customers requested region-level assurances during profile publish; this reduces blast radius and speeds detection of hardware-specific regressions (e.g., quantization kernels on Ampere vs Habana).
acceptance_criteria: Can create a region-specific publish job with explicit time window (start/end) in Console and via API
Can configure canary fractions per region (mirror %, direct %) and a shadow traffic toggle
Automated gates exist: (1) latency P99 threshold, (2) throughput drop threshold, (3) cost-per-token delta threshold; failing any gate pauses rollout
Dashboard shows per-region canary health and a one-click rollback that pins traffic back to previous profile
Runbook document created and validated with SRE and Customer Success for manual intervention steps
plan: Phase 1: API + Console controls for region/time-window/canary fractions (2 weeks). Phase 2: Telemetry gates and gating engine integration with rollout controller (3 weeks). Phase 3: Dashboard, runbook, and partner validation with 2 pilot customers across EU and APAC (2 weeks).
rollout_steps: Create API endpoint /publishProfiles with region/timezone/canary payload
Expose UI in Console under Performance Profiles -> Publish (region and timezone fields)
Wire gating engine to ingest per-region telemetry feeds and evaluate thresholds every 2 minutes
Start pilot publish to EU region for 2 customers (mirror 30%, direct 5%) and monitor 48h
If gates pass, automatically increase direct fraction to 50% over 6 hours; if any gate trips, rollback and notify stakeholders
telemetry_requirements: Per-region P50/P95/P99 latency for each endpoint and model variant
Throughput (requests/sec) and served tokens/sec pre/post publish
Cost-per-token estimation computed by profile and runtime variant
Error rates (5xx/4xx) and tail latency for first byte
Alerting rules: P99 > baseline * 1.25 or throughput drop > 15% triggers pause
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: False positives in gates due to transient infra noise. Mitigation: require sustained violation over 3 consecutive 2-minute windows before pausing.
Risk: Customer confusion when a profile is rolled back regionally. Mitigation: send automated customer notification + include rollback rationale in Console timeline.
Risk: Timezone scheduling conflicts with SRE on-call. Mitigation: default publish windows to 02:00-06:00 local time with opt-out and explicit approval flow.
next_steps: 1) Align on telemetry thresholds with Runtime Eng (by 2026-03-18). 2) PR for publish API spec and Console mockups (target 2026-03-20). 3) Recruit two pilot customers for EU and APAC pilots (target sign-off 2026-03-22).
